differences.what: the street front's openings: the attic's paired lights, the pavilion's second-storey window, the door, the narrow light over its south jamb and the principal-storey window past the tree
differences.how: T-3156: the camera fitted to them (11.7 px rms); the render's openings fall within about 0.5 m of the print's, the attic's the furthest (the pavilion's place, below)

differences.what: the pavilion carried up an attic storey with its paired transomed lights under its own steep hipped roof, the roof running back into the mansard
differences.how: T-3156: the shallow pavilion's attic storey and K01's hipped crown raised onto it

differences.what: the pavilion and its attic stand about 0.5-0.7 m north of the print's, because K01 cannot cut the door through a projection (as on the square-on)

the corner bay runs about 0.75 m south of the main front's south corner: the print's cornice turns onto the flank at x 1605 px and the bay's south face shows at x 1745-1790 px; the build sets the bay flush with the flank (its corner at x 1618 px, the main corner at 1711)
the south flank is rock-faced random ashlar, dark against the smooth front; the build lays it in buff common brick
differences.how: T-3562: the flank laid in the front's K02 stone on the front's own beds, rock-faced to the profile's 25 mm (stone_front.flanks), its windows under flat arches and seated on stone sills; it renders as a broken stone face against the smooth front where it rendered buff brick. The print's broken-coursed random ashlar is laid as even courses on the front's lines: the joint pattern, under a visitor's notice

differences.what: the south flank's tall stack, carried up from the flank wall past the mansard with a panelled shaft and a corbelled head of flues (x 1740-1820 px)
differences.how: T-3561: rebuilt as the print's: K15's stone stack standing on the south cornice about 1.6 m back from the front, rising past the mansard to a corbelled head and cap at 14.45 m, with three tall pots in a row back from the street to about 15.2 m; measured from the cornice's corner it renders 83 px along the flank against the print's 73 px, and its pots' tops at y 75 px against 72 px

differences.what: the mansard's curb and cresting: the print's curb, under its cresting, stands about 0.8 m higher on this view than the build's; and the gabled dormer on the south flank's mansard (x 1820-1880 px), built by T-3562 just behind the stack (13.9 m from the rear, where it stood out of frame at 9.0 m), its sash and gable about 1 m lower than the print's with the curb
differences.how: T-3562 lays the K10 kit's 0.45 m iron cresting on the street and south flank curbs and the cross on the pavilion's crown (the square-on's record); they render on the build's curb and crown, so the curb's height stays the open question here and on the square-on (its deck)

differences.what: the main cornice's stone consoles, round the corner onto the flank
differences.how: T-3561: K10's scrolled consoles (wall_head.blocks) under the corona, 0.45 m high, 0.17 m wide, no more than 0.5 m apart, on a 0.32 m frieze; they render at y 405-440 px against the print's 400-432 px, and carry round the south-west corner and along the south flank as the oblique draws them

differences.what: the door's pedimented hood and the stoop's stone cheeks
differences.how: T-3562: the stone pediment on its brackets over the door, and the swept cheeks with a newel at each foot, as on the square-on (whose print shows both whole); here the tree's trunk crosses the hood

differences.what: the stoop's open south side (x 1080-1340 px, y 980-1160 px): the landing on a square pier at its outer corner and open beneath back to the wall, black under a soffit about 0.3 m deep, and the flight carried off the pier on a rampant arch from 0.82 m over grade down to grade about 0.9 m along the run; built by T-3562 (K07's arched swept cheek), the void closed in the kit's dark backing
the iron hand rail on the stoop's south cheek, the cheek's stepped top under it where the build's sweeps, and the basement doorway in the wall under the landing (x 1045-1260 px, y 960-1150 px)
the stone balcony's pierced panels on the bay's deck
differences.how: the panels' pattern is K08's, the rail's place and height the print's within a few pixels

differences.what: the stone's colour and tone
the street fence, the walk and the parkway's posts
the coping, posts and walk T-3206 lays
differences.how: seen obliquely the low coping and posts read as the print's low line; read square-on in chicagology_square_on

differences.what: the stack's sunk panels on its south face (x 1765-1825 px, about 11.35-13.45 m)
differences.how: T-3562: built. Three narrow panels (0.15 m across, 0.05 m deep) sunk in the stack's south face from 11.35 m to 13.45 m, 0.3 m under the corbelled head, where the print draws three dark lines evenly across the shaded face (x 1765-1825 px). The stack stands on the flank's cornice clear of the mansard, so its panels run below the roof's highest covering under it (panel_foot_m); K15 now sinks a stone stack's panel in its own stone, so they read as stone and not as brick strips. The render draws the three beside the print's within a few pixels in height and run; the build's stack stands right of the print's with the south wall's open set-out, as before

differences.what: the stack's pots: the print's stand about 1.0-1.2 m over the cap, slender and fluted, in a row back from the street
differences.how: T-3562: K15 gains a long pot, 1.1 m high and slimmer than the tall one (0.12 m at its foot, 0.08 m in its shaft, a 0.1 m lip), and the south stack names it (pot: long) on its three flues; all 52 K01 houses were rebuilt, 51 of them byte-identical, only their input hashes moved. Against the head (cap's top to the corbels' foot, 0.7 m) the build's pots now stand 1.24 times its height and the print's about 1.4 times, about 0.1-0.15 m apart, inside the bar (the kit's 0.72 m tall pot stood 0.3-0.5 m short). Their fluting is under the bar

differences.what: a fourth pot: a pale shape nearest the street on the stack's head (x 1717-1740 px, y 72-130 px), lit on its west side with a rim at its top, may be a fourth pot in the row or the head's lit side
differences.how: the build keeps three: four of K15's 0.21 m flues need a 1.24 m face and the stack is 1.1 m along the flank as both prints read it (the flue spacing rule in k01_frontage_params._k15_heads), so a fourth pot is a wider stack or a smaller flue, and the shape's reading is not settled

differences.what: the band under the stack's head: the build's K15 soot band lays the top 0.45 m of the shaft under the corbels in dark brick, which renders red on this stone stack; the print shows the head's pale stone and its shadowed mouldings there (x 1730-1830 px, y 140-185 px)
differences.how: T-3562: K15's soot band is a brick stack's; a stone stack now keeps its own stone up to its corbelled head (k15_chimneys.stack_solids), so the top 0.45 m of the shaft renders in the stack's stone where the brick band rendered red; the print's shadowed mouldings are the head's corbel courses, which the build carries. 1815 is the only K01 house on a stone K15 stack: the other 51 were rebuilt byte-identical, only their input hashes moved

differences.what: the rosettes over the cornice's consoles
differences.how: carved bosses about 0.12 m across in the cornice's bed, under the 0.3 m bar; not built

differences.what: the south flank's tone: the print draws the rock-faced flank darker than the front; a monochrome print cannot say whether that is another stone, soot or the light
differences.how: T-3562 lays it in the front's Lemont stone (L-k01-1815-sears-1893)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
